title: Unlocalized linear presentation after scalar extension killing pi
statement: Let $R,C$ be commutative rings, $\pi\in R$, $R_2=R/(\pi^2)$, and $d$ the polynomial data of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-preparation]. Let $B$ be a compatible $R$- and $R_2$-algebra with $\pi=0$ in $B$. Fix $k<d.r$. Set $Q=R[x_i,z_l]$ and $J_k=(f_l-\pi z_l,a_kz_l-\sum_{j\in E_k}h_{klj}z_j-\pi g_{kl}:l<d.m)$. Set $A=R_2[x_i]/(\overline f_l)$ and $L=B\otimes_{R_2}A$. Let $\beta:R[x_i]\to L$ be coefficient reduction followed by quotient and right tensor inclusion. Let $I=(\beta(a_k)z_l-\sum_{j\in E_k}\beta(h_{klj})z_j:l<d.m)$ in $L[z_l]$. There is a $B$-algebra isomorphism $e:L[z_l]/I\to B\otimes_R\operatorname{ULift}(Q/J_k)$ satisfying $e([\beta(p)])=1\otimes[p(x)]$ for every $p\in R[x_i]$. Polynomial rings, quotients and tensor products are as in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No localization or normalization is assumed.

proof.text: Use the canonical ULift equivalence and the tensor-quotient equivalence to identify the base-changed quotient with B[x,z] modulo the images of the original equations. Since pi maps to zero, those equations are f_l and the displayed homogeneous linear relations.

Split the variables x,z by the polynomial universal property. First quotient the coefficient ring by the f_l. Polynomial evaluation and quotient uniqueness identify the result with the polynomial ring over B[x]/(f_l), modulo the remaining linear relations.

Because the R-action on B factors through R_2, polynomial scalar extension and the tensor-quotient universal property identify B[x]/(f_l) with L=B tensor_R2 A. The forward and reverse maps fix coefficients and the original variables. The induced maps of polynomial quotients fix B and each z. Checking the composites on these generators proves the isomorphism and its coefficient compatibility.

theorem zero_base_single_chart_unlocalized (R : Type a) (Cbar : Type c)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Cbar] (π : R)
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) Cbar]
    (d : PopescuLiftPresentation R Cbar π)
    (B : Type b) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) B]
    [IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)) B]
    (hπ : algebraMap R B π = 0) (k : Fin d.r) :
    let J : Ideal d.polynomial := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin d.m ⊕ Fin d.m ↦
      match i with
      | .inl j => d.equation (.inl j)
      | .inr l => d.equation (.inr (k, l))))
    let L := B ⊗[R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)] d.reducedQuotient
    let β : MvPolynomial (Fin d.n) R →+* L :=
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R ⧸ Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R))
        (A := B)).toRingHom.comp ((Ideal.Quotient.mk d.reducedIdeal).comp
          (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({π ^ 2} : Set R)))))
    let I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d.m) L) := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun l ↦
      MvPolynomial.C (β (d.a k)) * MvPolynomial.X l -
        ∑ j : d.E k, MvPolynomial.C (β (d.h k l j)) * MvPolynomial.X (j : Fin d.m)))
    ∃ e : (MvPolynomial (Fin d.m) L ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[B]
        B ⊗[R] ULift (d.polynomial ⧸ J),
      ∀ p : MvPolynomial (Fin d.n) R,
        e (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.C (β p))) =
          Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := B)
            (ULift.up (Ideal.Quotient.mk J (d.includeX p)))
